value: A thicker conductor slows the wave on it: the Army's antenna manual says the wave's velocity falls as the conductor's circumference grows. A slower wave has a shorter wavelength, so a conductor of the same physical length holds more of it and is electrically longer.
reason: Never said why thickness adds electrical length. TM 11-666 par. 36c: 'As the circumference of the antenna increases, the wave velocity is lowered'; 36b: slower wave, shorter wavelength.

value: A paper on the US space agency's report server puts the electron mobility of GaAs at 3 to 5 times that of silicon, which allows faster switching in devices made from it; that speed is why it suits UHF and higher frequencies.
reason: Restated the pool. NASA NTRS 19910016619: 'its electron mobility is 3 to 5 times that of silicon, this allows for faster switching times'.

value: Through-hole means the leads pass through holes in the board and are soldered from one side of it to the other; the DIP was designed to be inserted into mounting boards in this way. The pool keys none of the other three as through-hole.
reason: Restated the key. NEETS Module 14 p. 3-10 (lead terminations) and p. 1-22 (DIP 'inserting packages into mounting boards'). No public-domain source found saying PLCC, BGA and SOT are surface-mount, so the card does not claim it.

value: The US space agency's gallium nitride report lists high-frequency operation among its advantages over silicon. Of the other options, silicon dioxide is used in microcircuits as a dielectric, not as the transistor material.
reason: Gave no reason. NASA NTRS 20205007412 executive summary: advantages over silicon include 'high frequency operation'; NEETS Module 14 p. 1-16: silicon dioxide among 'most commonly used dielectric materials'.

value: An empty capacitor acts as a short circuit at the first instant, so filter capacitors connected straight across a high voltage draw a surge of charging current. A step-start circuit limits that current at switch-on, so the capacitors charge gradually.
reason: Held patch, now sourced: NEETS Module 2 p. 3-8 ('when a capacitor is connected across a voltage source, a surge of charging current flows') and Module 9 ('the capacitor being a short at the first instant').

value: Air just above a large body of water can hold more moisture than normal, which then falls off quickly with height. Like a temperature inversion, this bends the wave more and can form a duct that carries microwaves hop by hop.
reason: Did not say why water. NEETS Module 18 p. 1-17: over 'large bodies of water' moisture lapse, alone or with inversion, causes ducting.

value: A quarter-wave matching section needs a characteristic impedance equal to the square root of the product of the two impedances it joins: √(100 × 50) ≈ 71 ohms, and 75 ohms is the nearest line offered.
reason: Only said the pool keys 75 ohms. TM 11-666 par. 86: Q-matching section impedance 'equal to the square root of the product'.

value: A: 50-ohm line would leave the mismatch where it is. B and D: 62 and 90 ohms are further than 75 ohms from the 71 ohms the rule gives.
